newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Anagram Finance offers 1:1 bonus.
newsitem.headline: India's Anagram Finance offers 1:1 bonus.

text.p: India' Anagram Finance Ltd, part of the Lalbhai group, has offered a bonus issue of 1:1, a company statement said.

The company also announced a dividend of four rupees on each share for the year 1995/96 (July/June) after it reported a net profit of 446.99 million rupees, up from 286.22 million in the previous year.
"The spectacular performance by Anagram comes in a year considered adverse for the financial services industry at large," the statement said.
It said during 1995/96 (July-June) the company's total income was up 46.44 percent to 1.98 billion rupees from 1.35 billion in the previous year.

"The company's well-defined retail strategy of offering simple retail products like car finance and truck finance through a powerful distribution system has paid off," the statement quoted the company's chairman Sanjay Lalbhai as saying.
Anagram Finance was also exploring the possibilities of entering into an alliance with a global insurance firm to enter into the sector once India gives permission to do so.
Currently, insurance is controlled by the state.
"In order to fuel its ambitious growth plans for 1996/97 the campany plans to float a bond issue very soon," the statement said.
